results: 1. Complete cranial-nerve and neurologic examination, including facial-nerve grading, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, smile, cheek puffing, and taste assessment
cranial nerve examination: bilateral post-paralytic facial synkinesis; narrowed left palpebral fissure
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
voice and hoarseness assessment: normal voice
gait, ability to run, and limb sensation: normal
2. Otoscopic examination of both ear canals and tympanic membranes
ear and mastoid examination: normal, no vesicles
3. Formal pure-tone audiometry with speech discrimination and tympanometry
4. MRI of the brain, cerebellopontine angles, and internal auditory canals with and without gadolinium contrast
MRI brain and internal auditory canal with contrast: no tumour, no perineural enhancement, no central lesion
5. Hemoglobin A1c and fasting blood glucose
6. Electrodiagnostic facial-nerve testing with electroneurography and needle electromyography
needle electromyography: chronic bilateral facial neuropathic changes with synkinesis
electroneuronography / facial EMG: chronic reinnervation with synkinetic co-activation; no active denervation
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Chronic bilateral post-paralytic facial synkinesis from prior recurrent idiopathic peripheral facial nerve palsy (bilateral Bell’s palsy)

ALTERNATIVE: Melkersson–Rosenthal syndrome

ALTERNATIVE: Lyme neuroborreliosis with prior bilateral facial palsy

ALTERNATIVE: Ramsay Hunt syndrome without rash (zoster sine herpete)
